title: add-jsonschema-response-format-strict-mode-and-validation
author: Arielle Mendoza
commits: feat(api): add response_format param and JSON Schema strict mode validation (Arielle)
feat(runtime): streaming validation hooks + structured error events (Kai)
chore(compat): map openai.response_format to native schema handler (Sofia)
test: add unit + integration tests for strict mode and fallback behaviors (Martin)
description:
Motivation: Provide first-class JSON Schema-based structured output support on the public API with an explicit strict mode that validates model output against a user-provided schema. This addresses two developer pain points: (1) silent schema mismatches when using response_format / JSON Schema, and (2) poor developer ergonomics when streaming structured output + handling validation failures.

What this PR does: Adds a new 'response_format' parameter to the Redwood API (and maps OpenAI-compatible response_format values to the native schema handler). Implements server-side JSON Schema validation during generation with a 'strict' option. When strict=true the runtime validates tokens as they stream and emits structured validation events on the stream for early feedback. If the final output fails validation, the server returns a deterministic validation error (error.code=validation_error) with a JSON path, failing constraint, and a short human-friendly message. The compatibility layer for OpenAI-style calls now accepts response_format: {type: 'json_schema', schema: <json> , mode: 'strict'|'lax'} and translates it to the native handler so clients using the OpenAI shim get the same semantics.

Key behaviors: 
- Lax mode (default): existing behavior preserved - we attach best-effort schema hints but do not fail the request; the response is the model output. We include a validation summary in the final API metadata when mismatches are detected.
- Strict mode: the runtime validates incremental parse trees as tokens arrive. When a token causes a temporary parse error (partial JSON parse failure), we do not immediately fail; we buffer up to a small lookahead. When a definitive schema violation is detected we emit a structured stream event: {event: 'validation_error', code: 'validation_error', path: '/choices/0/message/content', rule: 'type', expected: 'object', found: 'string', message: 'expected object at path /items[2]'} so clients can handle it in real time. The final RPC returns HTTP 422 with machine-readable details if the output cannot be reconciled.

Implementation notes: 
- runtime/streaming/validator.ts: incremental JSON parser + JSON Schema validator integration. Uses a streaming-safe subset of Ajv with a small validation sandbox to keep latency bounded. Validations run on the scheduler's worker thread and respect token budgets to avoid amplifying latency.
- api handler: response_format parsing, OpenAI mapping, header propagation for observability.
- observability: emits validation.metrics.{total,failures,latency} and tracing spans around validation.
- backward compatibility: default mode is 'lax' to avoid breaking existing customers. OpenAI shim recognizes both 'response_format' top-level and the legacy 'response_format.type=json_schema' query shapes.

Testing and QA: Added unit tests for incremental parsing and schema edge cases, end-to-end integration tests that validate streaming events and final 422 responses, and a canary run on perf-canary to measure tail latency (no measurable regression <1% p99 increase). CI runs include the new tests; flaky tests are isolated to the integration test group.

Migration notes for users: 
- If you opt-in to strict mode, be prepared to surface validation_error events client-side and handle HTTP 422 final responses. The SDKs (Python/TS/Go) will be updated in separate PRs to add helpers for stream-level validation events.

Related: ENG-2142 (design doc), ENG-2198 (openai compatibility mapping).

release_notes: Adds response_format JSON Schema support with a 'strict' validation mode that emits structured validation events during streaming and returns machine-readable validation errors for unrecoverable mismatches. Default mode remains lax to preserve backward compatibility. SDKs will follow up with helpers for handling validation events.
